Die Walküre
The Valkyrie
Ballet i 4 Akter af August Bournonville
Ballett in vier Akten von August Bournonville
Ballet in Four Acts by August Bournonville

history.p: "The Valkyrie" was August Bournonville's first full-length ballet based on a theme from Nordic mythology. When he conceived the idea in the autumn of 1851, he had asked Niels W. Gade to write the music. In 1860 however, when he started working on the project, he sent his programme for the ballet to Hartmann, who readily accepted to write the music, provided he got the necessary time. The music was composed in an exceptionally close collaboration between composer and choreographer right down to the smallest details. It was thus Bournonville who suggested that Hartmann reused parts of his music to Oehlenschläger's play "Olaf the Hellige" (HartW 11) and also the use of leit-motifes.

annot.p: In September 1861 Horneman & Erslev started publishing single numbers from the ballet in their periodical "Musikalsk Museum". From vol. 16 no. 2 to vol. 17 no. 6 in December 1862, 17 of the numbers from Act One to Act Three were published. In December 1862 these were accumulated to the first piano score, comprising 53 unnumbered pages, followed by Act Four with pages 54-73. It was published at the beginning of 1863 with the printed remark: "1ste (-3die) Gratis-Levering til 17de Aargang af 'Musikalsk Museum'.". In this edition following numbers are missing: 4, 7, 13, 14b, 15, 16b and 19.
